title: Independent K2 labels in Upper Sco, the Pleiades and Praesepe confirm the age decline of complex periodic variables and agree with contraction if the rate falls as a power law of R_cor/R*
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. Earlier TESS work found that the CPV rate falls with age at fixed period, and that the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x = R_cor/R* (BHAC15 radii) explains the decline. We tested this with independent data: published expert K2 labels (scallop shells and persistent flux dips) in Upper Sco (16 of 150 stars, 0.15-1 d), the Pleiades (5 of 351) and Praesepe (0 of 128). We applied TESS rate laws with a K2 efficiency from injected TESS CPV shapes, blurred by the 29.4-min K2 integration. A law with no age decline predicts a Pleiades/Upper Sco ratio of 2.75; we observe 0.31 (p = 5e-6). It predicts 13 Praesepe CPVs; we observe 0. A contraction law fitted to 1-24 Myr TESS stars, with a constant rate below x = 2 and a power law above it (slope -4.6 +/- 0.9), predicts a ratio of 0.54 (0.34-0.89; p = 0.23). It also puts the older TESS and K2 CPVs at the observed x values. The earlier quadratic form in log x fails this position test (p = 0.0012 TESS, 0.008 Pleiades), because older CPVs extend to x = 5-8 where young stars are rare. With photometric radii, the young laws pass, and an age term at fixed period fails in the Pleiades (p = 0.003). In both K2 clusters, CPV-like hosts are brighter than the cluster sequence (rate x4.2 per magnitude, p = 4e-5), also in Gaia with RUWE <= 1.4 in Upper Sco. Limitations: only 5 Pleiades and 17 older TESS CPVs; the K2 and TESS labels come from different vetters, so we use ratios; the young-law shape is not constrained at x > 5; Gaia cannot detect equal-mass binaries; no spectra.
